edges.description: The premature termination codon triggers nonsense-mediated decay, so patient fibroblasts have greatly reduced ARNT2 transcript and little or no detectable protein.
Without ARNT2 protein the SIM1-ARNT2 heterodimer cannot form, so SIM1/ARNT2-dependent developmental transcription fails.

Loss of SIM1-ARNT2 activity blocks terminal differentiation of magnocellular and parvocellular neurosecretory neurons in the paraventricular and supraoptic nuclei. Demonstrated in Arnt2-null mice and inferred in humans from the parallel endocrine phenotype.
ARNT2 is expressed in the developing and post-natal cortex; its loss impairs post-natal brain growth and myelination. The specific target genes in human forebrain are not established.
ARNT2 is expressed in the developing neural retina and post-retinal visual pathway; its loss produces post-retinal/chiasmal visual dysfunction with preserved retinal responses.

ARNT2 is expressed in the developing renal tubules; its loss is associated with congenital anomalies of the kidneys and urinary tract. The direct-versus-neurogenic contribution to bladder dysfunction is not resolved.

edges.description: Loss of magnocellular vasopressin neurons produces arginine-vasopressin deficiency and central diabetes insipidus, presenting neonatally with hypernatraemia.
Deficient hypothalamic CRH drive produces ACTH deficiency and central (secondary) adrenal insufficiency, a life-threatening neonatal finding.
Deficient hypothalamic TRH drive gives central hypothyroidism in a majority of affected children.
Abnormal growth-hormone secretion and growth failure follow from hypothalamo-pituitary dysfunction; one child met criteria for growth hormone deficiency.
Gonadotropin deficiency reflects the hypothalamo-pituitary axis defect; the affected male had undescended testes with low LH and FSH.
Bilateral undescended testes in the affected male accompany the gonadotropin deficiency.
The combined multiple pituitary hormone deficiencies amount to panhypopituitarism, as seen in the longest-surviving reported patient.
Deficient hypothalamic trophic drive is accompanied by a structurally hypoplastic anterior pituitary with an absent posterior bright spot and thin stalk on MRI.
Hypothalamic insufficiency from abnormal paraventricular nucleus development is the authors' interpretation of the obesity, alongside the endocrine deficits.
The thin pituitary stalk is part of the hypothalamo-pituitary MRI pattern that accompanies the neurosecretory defect.
The absent posterior pituitary bright spot is part of the same hypothalamo-pituitary MRI pattern and accompanies the vasopressin deficiency.
Progressive failure of post-natal brain growth produces acquired (secondary) microcephaly in all affected children despite normal head size at birth.
Impaired forebrain development produces severe global developmental delay.
Generalized tonic-clonic and partial seizures occur in affected children, with onset from 8 days to 1 year.
All affected children develop total-body spastic cerebral palsy (GMFCS grade V).
A global delay in brain myelination accompanies the frontotemporal hypoplasia.
A thin corpus callosum is part of the shared MRI pattern.
Frontal lobe hypoplasia is part of the shared MRI pattern of impaired forebrain development.
Temporal lobe hypoplasia is part of the shared MRI pattern of impaired forebrain development.
Post-retinal and chiasmal dysfunction produces cortical/cerebral visual impairment despite preserved retinal responses.
Hydronephrosis, usually bilateral, is part of the congenital urinary-tract phenotype.

nodes.description: Failure of SIM1-ARNT2 transcription leaves the paraventricular and supraoptic nuclei hypocellular and lacking terminally differentiated neurosecretory neurons, so the hypothalamic hormones that drive the anterior pituitary (CRH, TRH, somatostatin) and the posterior pituitary (vasopressin, oxytocin) are deficient. This underlies the congenital hypothalamo-pituitary insufficiency of WEDAS.
